%1$s is ready, protected with your passphrase. It’s a snapshot of today; make a new one whenever you like, and it will replace the older copy when your family opens it.
Can’t keep this keepsake on the device.

A Keepsake Bible is a copy of your highlights and notes that your family can open in Scripture Alone and read as you marked it — the way a well-worn Bible gets passed down. It’s a single file you keep and give however you like: Quick Share, Messages, a USB drive, or with your papers.
Your name, as family knows you
The dedication opens their copy — a few words to whoever reads it next. The translation is the one it opens in.
Write the passphrase down exactly as shown and keep it with the file — for example, with your will. Without it, no one can open this keepsake: not your family, and not us. There is no reset.
Without a passphrase, anyone who has the file can read it, like a Bible on a shelf. That’s usually what you want for family. Add one if the file might travel somewhere less private.
Nothing on this device can receive it.
Whoever made it chose a passphrase so only family could open it. It may be written down with the file, or with their papers.
Kept on this device, separate from your own highlights and notes. It’s read-only; nothing in it can be changed.
You’ll find it again under Appearance → Keepsake & Export.
There are no notes on this chapter.
Give your family a copy of your highlights and notes — a digital version of the Bible you’ve marked over the years. It’s a file you hand over yourself; nothing is sent anywhere.
When someone gives you a Keepsake Bible, open the file here — or tap it in Messages, Gmail or Files. It stays on this device, apart from your own notes.
Tap one to read it. Their highlights and notes appear in the text, just as they left them. Touch and hold for more.
If you’ve been reading in Life Bible — the app formerly called Tecarta Bible — your notes, highlights and saved verses can come with you.

A keepsake is a snapshot. Notes you write afterwards aren’t in it — when you’d like your family to have them, make a new keepsake. Opening a newer one replaces the older copy on their device.
Keepsakes are ordinary files: a ZIP archive of readable text. Even without this app, the words stay recoverable.
The keepsake will be removed from this device. If you want it again later, you’ll need the original file.

I can’t fix what I don’t know about. If something is broken, confusing, or missing, email me — one person reads every message, and a fix for you is a fix for everyone.
Built by one person, same care
Scripture Alone is made by one person, with no ads, no tracking, and no venture money behind it. A rating takes ten seconds and genuinely decides whether anyone else ever sees it.
No accounts, no tracking, no ads — nothing you do in Scripture Alone is sent anywhere unless you send it yourself.

That’s everything attached — no identifiers, no location, no logs. Delete any line you’d rather not send.
Scripture Alone on iPhone reads in Apple’s own faces. Apple licenses them for its devices only, so on Android each is replaced by an open-licensed face of the same kind.
